contract_inferred: No 00-contract.md. Inferred from the page: web, Persuade with Experience (the site of an open-source design skill, built around large before-and-after page screenshots, a theme gallery with filters, example builds, an FAQ accordion and an install block with copy buttons). English only (html lang en at every width), no market named. No right-to-left language. The screenshots are the product's evidence, so image weight is partly the content.
overall_reason: The static page reads with scripts off and its layout holds at every width, but 73% of the text waits on an IntersectionObserver to appear, and theme images are served at 1,440px into slots as small as 28px.

score.reason: T-WIDTHS, T-HOSTILE-CONTENT and T-NO-SCRIPT pass, but T-HIDDEN-CONTENT fails when the observer never fires (ROB-015, citing the sweep's ROB-001 Floor), T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB fails the image budget on unresized thumbnails (ROB-018), and T-TRUNCATION cuts one install command (ROB-006).

findings.title: Content and navigation do not depend on script
findings.where: Sections with div.wrap.reveal (comparison, 'It designs before it codes', themes, examples, Questions), observer never fires, all widths
findings.evidence: With an observer that never fires only 419 of 1,862 characters are visible (share 0.225); with scripts off 1,569 are visible (share 0.843), so the text is in the HTML and the reveal script hides it until IntersectionObserver fires (resilience.hidden_content). The sweep's hidden_content hit (ROB-001, Floor) records 1,121 characters (73%) invisible when the observer never fires. The how-it-works list carries the class 'is-armed' (ol.how.is-armed).
findings.before: Script arms each .reveal section as hidden on load and waits for the observer to show it.
findings.after: Arm the reveal only for sections below the fold after the observer reports them out of view, and add a timeout that shows every section after 2 s (draft ROB-204).
findings.why: A browser where the observer is throttled or fails (some in-app browsers, print, reader tools) shows a quarter of the page.

findings.title: Weight fits the page's job
findings.where: Theme gallery and example images (theme-furrow.webp, darkroom-photographer.webp, hedgerow-dog-walking.webp, theme-dose.webp), 1440px
findings.evidence: Images total 2,588 KiB over 37 files, past the 2,400 KiB fail budget (against_budgets image_kib fail). Ten images are served at 2.4 to 51 times their shown width, 867 KiB together: theme-furrow.webp (123 KiB) and darkroom-photographer.webp (117 KiB) are 1,440px wide and shown at 28px, and hedgerow-dog-walking.webp is 1,440px shown at 164px (performance.images.oversized_over_2.2x). The full-page comparison screenshot (fieldbook-hallmark-full.webp, 500 KiB) is the content the page exists to show.
findings.before: One 1,440px rendition of each theme screenshot, used for the full view, the cards and the small thumbnails.
findings.after: Keep the full comparison screenshots, and serve the theme and example cards through srcset at 1 and 2 times their shown widths (for example 200, 400 and 800px WebP) (draft ROB-167).
findings.why: A phone visitor pays nearly 0.9 MB for thumbnails drawn a few dozen pixels wide, on top of the screenshots that carry the argument.

findings.title: Wrap before truncating, and never truncate what matters
findings.where: Footer install block, dl.ag > div:nth-of-type(4) > dd > code ('Only this agent'), 375, 1280 and 1440px
findings.evidence: The command 'npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code' is nowrap with an ellipsis and clipped by 122px at 375, 45px at 1280 and 17px at 1440 (text_risk.nowrap_clipped). tiles/375-10.png shows 'npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --…' and tiles/1440-09.png 'npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-…'. A copy button sits beside it.
findings.before: A one-line command cut at its distinguishing flag at every width.
findings.after: Let the code line wrap (white-space: pre-wrap with overflow-wrap: anywhere) or scroll inside its own box, and keep the copy button.
findings.why: The cut part is the flag that names the agent, so a reader cannot see which agent the command installs for before running it.

strengths: With scripts off 84% of the text is visible and the page has 15 KiB of script, so it is static HTML at heart.

The layout holds at every width: the document width equals the viewport, the theme filter is its own horizontal scroller (div.seg overflow-x: auto) and the FAQ rows wrap their questions (tiles/375-05.png, tiles/375-08.png).
Headings carry overflow-wrap rules (h1, h2), 10 aspect-ratio rules reserve space for the screenshots, and 67 of 85 images are lazy-loaded.
The lab LCP is 440 ms over 47 requests.
not_investigated: T-STRESS: no hostile content was injected; long names were judged from layout evidence.
A right-to-left render and translated strings were not captured. The page uses physical properties almost only (46 physical against 4 logical); a readiness note for an English-only page.
The page load was not throttled and layout shift was not measured as a number (capture predates the CLS record).
T-FAILURE-PATH and T-SLOW-LINE: async found no primary actions; the copy buttons, the theme filters and the example wheel were not exercised.
T-EXTREME-COUNTS: the filter counts ('All 50', 'Editorial 20') are fixed catalog numbers.
The FAQ answers are behind closed accordions and were not opened.
One stylesheet was cross-origin and unreadable; its rules are unknown, not absent.
Widths between the captures, landscape, zoom at 200%, back navigation and deep links.
